structured_output.summary:
The tree has stopped keeping up with the results. There are three main problems.

1. **Tip provenance.** H2, H2.10.4 and H4.2.4 still treat the tip's provenance as an open question, even though E079, E081 and E083 could only have worked if the tip already had the Fable tail. That evidence settles H2.10.4 on its "tail already present" branch. It means the tail and the 24 px trim did not stack, and E068's +0.42 pp was mostly a lucky draw.
2. **Decisions made inside noise.** Most decisions since E070 rest on two effective runs or on single off-seed A/Bs. The off-seed instrument has never been calibrated, and its baseline (0.7530) is one sample that was rerun bit-identically. Paired off-seed differences probably carry about 0.15 pp of SE, so the -0.07, -0.18 and +0.11 pp verdicts are all roughly one SE or less.
3. **Statuses and mechanisms the results contradict.** Statuses and mechanisms no longer match the evidence:
   - H9.1.1 is still listed as open after E082 collapsed training.
   - H9.1 boils down to raising the Muon LR floor. That is a scalar knob, and E081/E083 already argue against it.
   - H2.14.4 is still ranked as a lever even though E076 closed it.
   - H8's claim that early training is the fragile part does not fit E084. A simpler story fits E043, E038, E022 and E084 alike: what matters is the total number of updates.

**The surprising result is E084.** Running the 32 px phase at bs 1024 gave +0.23 pp scored and +0.11 pp off-seed, at +2.5% time. It is confounded: the switch to sample-indexed scheduling stretched the final-EMA window from 8 to about 12 steps and moved the lookahead stop. It is also below its own pre-registered threshold (about 0.044 pp per 1% of time against 0.055). It still needs its second scoring and an ablation that separates the two causes.

**Never tried:**
- a fractional trim of the 32 px phase on any Muon base;
- the real whitening-bias detach (H2.15, which the tree ranks as its top time lever);
- any augmentation change under Muon;
- removing or retuning the SGD-era lookahead;
- ending training at 28 px and evaluating at 32 px (the FixRes direction);
- per-layer Muon lr.

**What the Lvl1 hypotheses fail to explain:**
- Why end-of-run averaging is so sensitive (-0.2 to -0.3 pp) while the LR floor does nothing. One candidate the tree has not considered: a mismatch between the averaged weights and the BN buffers copied from the net.
- Why some reruns are bit-identical and others diverge. H4.4.1 could answer this from existing logs at no cost, but it has never been checked.
- Whether time rankings measured on this 400 W SXM card carry over to the 300 W PCIe judge.

critiques.issue: The results have already settled the provenance question, but the tree still calls it unresolved and builds a reinterpretation on it. E079 removed the final EMA from the tip and lost 0.18 pp off-seed. E081 changed the tip's final-EMA window, and E083 replaced it. None of that is possible on code without a tail, and E081's description says the I083 drop note confirms e945ed5 contains it. So H2.10's claim that the 24 px trim cost only about 0.055 pp per 1% rests on a premise the evidence contradicts. The pessimistic reading holds: the tail and the trim did not stack. Against the tail pool, the 1.25@24 trim cost about 0.25 pp for about 2% of time. The other possibility is that the tail's +0.25 pp was mostly E068's high draw (0.7579 against E069's 0.7544). Also, five experiments (E077–E083) were run on a base described as 'verified' that nobody actually verified.
critiques.suggestion: Run the free git diff of e945ed5 against a1aef09 and 766d5bf now, before any scored run. If the tail is present, resolve H2.10.4 on its 'already present' branch, restore the 0.14 pp per 1% figure for low-res trims, and mark the tail's mean effect unconfirmed: its only evidence is one high draw plus E079's ablation, which was itself within noise. Change H2's statement to match.

critiques.issue: Since E077, the off-seed A/B decides nearly everything, but its noise has never been measured. The tip's off-seed 0.7530 is effectively one sample, because its rerun in E081 was bit-identical. A bit-identical rerun does not sample the training-divergence mode that H4.4 says is the noise that matters. The scale of that noise: per-seed rerun differences reach 0.2–0.6 pp (E028, E042), so the SE of a paired difference between 8-seed means is about 0.1–0.15 pp. On that scale, E077's -0.07, E078's and E079's -0.18 and E084's +0.11 are all within about 1.2 SE. Only E083's -0.29 approaches 2 SE.
critiques.suggestion: Before relying on it again, calibrate the instrument. Run the tip off-seed in a fresh process until you get at least one non-bit-identical sample, or two, and report the paired-difference sd. Then restate every off-seed verdict as a multiple of that SE. Do not call E079 'supports' or E077/E078 'refutes' on the off-seed evidence alone.

critiques.issue: This is the only positive structural result since E068, and it rests on one scored run (0.7560) and one off-seed run (+0.11 pp). It is confounded. The 'samples-indexed rewrite' keeps the final-EMA window and lookahead stop at the same sample count, so at bs 1024 the window is about 12 steps instead of 8. E081 showed that window length moves accuracy. The rewrite also changes the per-step SGD scaling in the 32 px phase. On off-seed it buys about 0.044 pp per 1% of time, below its own pre-registered threshold of 0.055. On scored runs it buys about 0.09 pp per 1%. The two instruments disagree on whether it passes.
critiques.suggestion: Run the pending second scoring first. Then ablate: bs 1024 at 32 px with the EMA window and lookahead stop fixed at 8 steps, rather than at an equal sample count. Judge it against the pre-registered 0.055 pp per 1% using the pooled scored and off-seed evidence. If it passes, pair it immediately with the 32 px trim (H2.10.5), because a gain in accuracy only matters if it funds a time cut.

critiques.issue: H9.1.1 is still listed as 'open' although E082 collapsed training (0.487). The mechanism is also broken in a deeper way. E082's own post-mortem establishes that for filters followed by BN, only lr/||w|| matters. So the proposed follow-up, decaying the target and the LR together, is a functional no-op. And hiverge's combined schedule, a relative step ending at about 0.3x, is the same as raising the Muon LR floor to about 0.3x. That is a scalar end-of-run knob, contradicting H9's claim that it is structural. It is also contradicted by E081 and E083: averaging iterates taken at higher LR hurt by 0.2–0.3 pp.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H9.1.1 refuted. Rewrite H9.1 as 'a higher late relative step (a Muon floor of about 0.15–0.3x)' and give it a low prior, since E057, E081 and E083 point the other way. Drop the no-op follow-up of decaying the target and the LR together.

critiques.issue: The split between structural and scalar changes is drawn after the fact, and the tree's own results contradict it. Head lr 0.5x is a scalar, and it is the one lever H6 says survived. E081 (EMA window), E083 (LAWA) and E082 (norm schedule) are structural by H9's own definition, and all three were negative by 0.1–0.3 pp, or collapsed training. As written, H9 tells the loop how to rank ideas, but no result could falsify it.
critiques.suggestion: Turn H9 into a falsifiable claim about update count. E043, E038, E022 and E084 are consistent with roughly +0.1 pp per +20–30% of optimizer steps, wherever in the run the steps are added. Predict the effect of the next step-count change from that slope, and retire the structural/scalar ranking rule.

critiques.issue: E084, where extra steps late in training helped, is evidence against early training being the special case. Together with E043, E038 and E022, a total-update-count story explains every remaining pillar of H8 except E032. E032 (no 24 px bridge) is just as easily explained by a sharp jump in resolution from 16 to 32 px as by early fragility.
critiques.suggestion: Retire H8 or fold it into an update-count hypothesis. Do not spend a run on H8.1.1. If anything, compare 'extra steps early' (bs 768 in the first 0.5 epoch) against 'extra steps late' (E084) at equal added step count.

critiques.issue: The +0.15–0.2 pp claim depends on two runs. The first is E066 at 0.7570; its Inductor flags count as math-neutral, but it is a high draw. The second is E049, on a different base. Without E066, E062/E063 pool to 0.7540 against a family of 0.7531, i.e. +0.09 pp, which is under 1 SE. E067 is bit-identical to E062 and counts only once. No off-seed comparison of 0.5x against 1x was ever run. 'The only scalar lever that survived' may itself be noise.
critiques.suggestion: Downgrade H7.3's confidence and state the effect as +0.09 to +0.19 pp (about 1 SE). It is free to keep, but do not use it as evidence that the head scale was a live knob, or to rank further head-side ideas.

critiques.issue: H6.5.2 is marked 'supported' on E068 alone (0.7579). The second run gave 0.7544, and the tail has never been checked off-seed against a no-tail version of the same schedule. H6.5.3 ran despite its gate (H2.10.4 showing an off-seed gain of at least 0.1 pp) never being met. E079 ('supports') rests on -0.18 pp off-seed and -0.15 pp scored, both about 1 SE. E079's time also rose 1% after removing work, which suggests that either time noise exceeds the stated ±0.6% or the change did more than specified.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H6.5.2 as inconclusive (mean effect). Report the per-seed sd for tail vs no-tail from the runs you already have (E068/E069 vs E062/E063), to test Fable's variance-reduction claim, which costs nothing. Diff E079 against the tip to explain its +1% time.

critiques.target: E081 / E083 interpretation ('averaging pre-floor iterates hurts')
critiques.issue: There is another explanation that has not been ruled out. Eval uses BN buffers copied from the net, and those match the final weights, not the averaged ones. A longer or uniform window moves the averaged weights further from the BN statistics, so accuracy could drop through a BN mismatch rather than because the averaged iterates were taken at higher LR. That would also explain why changing the floor (E057) is null while changing the window costs 0.2–0.3 pp.
critiques.suggestion: Add this to H6.5 as a competing mechanism. Discriminating test, untimed and off-seed only: the 20-step EMA of E081 with BN buffers averaged alongside the weights, or with a short BN re-estimation. If the loss disappears, the mechanism is BN mismatch and not the LR of the averaged iterates.

critiques.issue: The two levers H2 ranks highest have never been run. A fractional trim of the 32 px phase, which is about 71% of time, has never been tested on any Muon base. Its supposed 'binding' status rests only on E025, which used an older base and whole-epoch moves. The whitening-bias detach (H2.15.1) is a FLOP lever expected to save 1–2.5%. Instead, the last eight experiments went into scalar or averaging variants with low priors.
critiques.suggestion: Next queue, after the provenance diff: (1) H2.15.1, checking the compiled backward graph for the missing dgrad before scoring; (2) H2.10.5 at -0.25 epoch of 32 px, with E084's bs-1024 tail as its accuracy funding if E084 holds up.

critiques.issue: E076's outcome says the trial-1 penalty comes from a time window after build returns, and closes it. Yet H2.14.4 is still open and ranked as lever (c). If the window really is time-based ('any activity clears it'), a pinned staging buffer may not change anything.
critiques.suggestion: Close it, or rewrite the prediction to depend explicitly on whether the slow window is specific to pageable memory, and give it a gain of at most 0.6% that needs two runs to see.

Add a Lvl2 under H2 for a reduced-resolution tail (e.g. 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 3@32 + 1@28, or a 28 px tail entirely). Add a lookahead-removal arm, which is both an accuracy and a time lever, under H2.4. Rate both above the remaining scalar candidates (H6.7, H7.1.3).

critiques.issue: Both analyses are free and both are still open. The weight checksums and cuDNN kernel names were requested in E062, E067 and E081. Meanwhile, decisions keep pooling runs that may share a per-run offset. Some runs are tight (E063: 0.7543–0.7548; E074: 0.7555–0.7560) and others wide (E075: 0.7512–0.7570), which fits H4.5.
critiques.suggestion: Analyze the logged checksums and kernel sets before the next scored run. If kernel sets predict the run mean, pooling should be done per kernel set, and picks could be restricted in build without setting deterministic=True.

critiques.target: H2.4 (32 px phase is energy-bound, so per-step levers don't matter)
critiques.issue: E084 added about 66 steps at 32 px and cost +2.5% (about 0.11 s, roughly 1.7 ms per step), close to Muon's per-step cost. So per-step optimizer work does cost time in the capped 32 px phase too. It costs energy rather than idle gaps, but H2.4/H7.2 present Muon per-step cost as a lever only at 16 px.
critiques.suggestion: Update H2.4/H7.2: under the power cap, per-step Muon and lookahead work is roughly 1.7 ms of energy-equivalent time at any resolution. Per-step savings in the 32 px phase (lookahead removal, a cheaper renorm) are therefore live levers and should transfer to the 300 W judge.
